territorial_scope.description: Applies to telecommunications service providers of collective interest regulated by Anatel in Brazil, with some duties applied to operators named by Anatel ordinance.

evidence.quote: As disposições deste Regulamento aplicam-se a todas as prestadoras dos serviços de telecomunicações de interesse coletivo, ressalvadas as de Pequeno Porte

summary.short: Approves Anatel's R-Ciber regulation on cybersecurity for telecommunications service providers of collective interest, excluding small-size providers, requiring a cybersecurity policy, incident notification and vulnerability assessments; effective 4 January 2021.
summary.long: Approves the Regulamento de Segurança Cibernética Aplicada ao Setor de Telecomunicações (R-Ciber), adopted by Anatel's Conselho Diretor and in force from 4 January 2021. It applies to telecommunications service providers of collective interest other than small-size providers (Art. 2). Providers must maintain a cybersecurity policy approved by their board, with a non-sensitive extract published online (Arts. 6, 13-15), use suppliers with compatible policies and periodic independent audits (Art. 7), change default authentication on equipment lent to users (Art. 8), notify Anatel of relevant incidents and communicate them to other providers and users (Arts. 9, 17), commission independent vulnerability assessments (Arts. 10, 19), send data on critical telecommunications infrastructure (Arts. 11, 20), and file an annual report (Art. 16). Resolution 767/2024 extended Art. 8 to small providers (Art. 2-A) and applied some duties to operators identified in a Superintendency ordinance (Art. 2-B). The regulation creates the GT-Ciber working group (Art. 24) and lets Anatel impose specific technical requirements (Art. 23). Infringements are subject to sanctions under Lei 9.472/1997 and Anatel's sanctions regulation (Art. 25). Providers have 180 days from entry into force to comply (Art. 27).
